Author: Pankaj Purohit Bench: Pankaj Purohit  Office Notes,
 reports, orders or SL. proceedings or  Date COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS No directions and  Registrar's order

with Signatures  WPCRL No.856 of 2025  Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Tapan Singh, learned counsel for the petitioners.

2. Mr. S.C. Dumka, learned A.G.A. with Ms. Sweta Badola Dobhal, learned Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand/ respondent Nos.1 and 2.
3.

By means of the present writ petition, the petitioners have put to challenge the FIR No.0373 of 2024 dated 27.07.2024 for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468 and 471 IPC,
registered with P.S. Gangnahar, District Haridwar.

4. It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioners that the respondent No.3 executed the sale deeds of the plots in favour of petitioner No.1 on 19.03.2021 and sale deed of the house on 22.09.2021, and thereafter, with the help of then SHO, P.S. Kotwali Gangnahar Shr. Govind Kumar,
succeeded to got execute the sale deed of the aforesaid plot on 12.03.2024 in favour of her husband,
without any sale consideration and grabbed the all sale consideration of aforesaid plots and filed an application before S.P. Rural, Roorkee on 06.07.2024, in which the police after investigation,
submitted its report on 18.07.2024, wherein, it has been mentioned that the respondent No.3 is a greedy lady and filed the application of the basis of false allegations against the petitioners.

5. He further submits that thereafter, the respondent No.3 after making some improvement in her complaint, lodged the impugned FIR against the petitioners on 27.07.2024, in which also the IO after investigation, submitted final report on 10.10.2024.
But, respondent No.3 succeeded to get an order to re- investigate the matter from SSP, Haridwar.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner further contends that the petitioners have falsely been implicated in the aforesaid crime and they have no criminal history.
He also contends that petitioners earlier also cooperated with the investigation and now, also are ready to cooperate with the investigation.

He further submits that the Investigating Office without investigating the matter,
threatening the petitioners to arrest, which causes serious prejudice to petitioners, which is against WPCRL/856/2025 on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5496442/
1 the principle of natural justice.

7. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and having gone through the impugned FIR,
this Court thinks that the matter requires some deliberation.

8. Issue notice to respondent No.3, returnable within four weeks.
9.
Steps to be taken within a week.
Meanwhile, respondents may file counter affidavit(s).
12. Till the next date of listing, no coercive measure shall be taken against the petitioners pursuant to the aforesaid FIR provided they cooperate with the investigation.
13. Interim Relief Application (IA/1/2025) stands disposed of.

(Pankaj Purohit, J.) 08.08.2025 PN WPCRL/856/2025 on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5496442/
